subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots continue inheriting all host pnpm workspace overrides, or should OpenClaw scope/filter host overrides so plugin-owned dependency ranges such as Express 4's path-to-regexp@0.1.x remain intact?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent fix changes the dependency-ownership boundary between OpenClaw's security override policy and third-party plugin package graphs.

options.title: Scope managed-root overrides
options.body: Filter or namespace host overrides so OpenClaw security pins do not force incompatible transitive versions into plugin-owned dependency graphs, with regression coverage for Express 4 and core Express 5.

options.title: Validator-only warning
options.body: Keep host override propagation but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts during install and fail with a clear remediation message for plugin authors or operators.

options.title: Leave to plugin packages
options.body: Treat the issue as downstream-owned and require affected plugins to ship their own overrides or migrate to Express 5, accepting fragile user workarounds after forced reinstalls.

recommendation.title: Scope managed-root overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or namespace host overrides so OpenClaw security pins do not force incompatible transitive versions into plugin-owned dependency graphs, with regression coverage for Express 4 and core Express 5.

likelyOwner.reason: The current managed npm override propagation and workspace override history point to this area owner as the best available decision router.
